status_note: benchmark not built: free official inputs are partial and mostly proxies. Sourced: grid intensity (CEA CO2 baseline database xlsx, Ember), car stock 1991-2020 (MoRTH Road Transport Year Book Table 2.1, data.gov.in GODL API to 2017), NDC anchor (2022 updated NDC, intensity target only). Missing or proxy-only: passenger-car CO2 (UNFCCC BUR/BTR give whole road transport at 2016, 2020, 2022 only, no car split; BTR1 CRT xlsx must be fetched by hand from unfccc.int/documents/656940), annual km per car (no survey; Goel et al. 2015 Delhi 12,200 km), vehicle age (none published), certified technology by model (BEE CAFE reports OEM averages only; MIDC cycle). S2 would be FLAG (no absolute or sector target). More than half the inputs proxied, so any result would be direction-only under guideline 5.3. Model-level sales are not free: Hyundai Motor India and Kia India publish company totals only, SIAM model data is paid, Vahan's public report hides the model and exports by hand behind a CAPTCHA.

benchmark and cohorts built on 2026-09-04, entirely from Japanese official statistics. Volumes: the JADA nameplate ranking (top 50 nameplates; kei vehicles and foreign brands excluded by the source, so Toyota's coverage of its own registered volume is 99.0 % in 2024 and Nissan's 57.4 %, having only four nameplates in the ranking). Technology: the MLIT fuel-economy list, which publishes CO2 emissions per kilometre per certified grade, read in two editions because the list carries only what is type-approved on its own date. Benchmark: the MLIT Motor Vehicle Fuel Consumption Survey for distance and implied stock, AIRIA for the published expected vehicle life, and the GIO/NIES inventory for road CO2 split by vehicle type. S2 is the GX 2040 target (73 % below fiscal 2013 by fiscal 2040), communicated as Japan's NDC. Not assessed: battery-electric units (no Japanese electricity-consumption rating is published), plug-in hybrids (no utility factor), the JPN Taxi (an LPG hybrid in a workbook this build does not read) and the Kicks (withdrawn before either edition on hand). Buses are not built: the distance survey bundles petrol buses into the car and special-vehicle rows.
